statement: A data protection officer who is an individual based in India is appointed by a formal appointment letter or governing-body resolution. The officer answers to the governing body, with the reporting line documented, and is named as the contact point for the grievance process. The officer reports to the governing body on each reporting cycle. Proof is the appointment record, the organization chart and the governing-body minutes.
why_asked: Without a named, senior and local officer, privacy duties have no owner and the regulator and individuals have no one to contact.
how_to_ask: Ask who holds the role, where they sit and to whom they report. Check the person is based in India and is named in the grievance process. Example probe: "Show me the appointment record and the last time the officer reported to the board."
question: Has your organization appointed a data protection officer based in India who answers to the governing body?
expected_evidence: Appointment letter or governing-body resolution; organization chart showing the reporting line; grievance process naming the officer as contact; governing-body minutes recording the officer's reports for the last reporting cycle.
good_looks_like: A named individual in India holds the role by formal appointment. The reporting line to the governing body is documented. The grievance process names the officer, and minutes show the officer reporting.
test: Obtain the appointment record and the organization chart. Check the person is an individual based in India, reports to the governing body and is named in the grievance process. Pass if all three hold and minutes from the last reporting cycle show the officer reporting.
baseline_risk: No one is accountable for privacy duties, and the regulator and individuals cannot reach a responsible person.
applicability: Applies if the organization is designated a significant data fiduciary.

statement: An independent data auditor is appointed under a documented engagement to evaluate the organization's compliance with its data protection duties. The auditor has no role in the processing or in designing the controls under audit, and signs a declaration of independence. The auditor issues a report on each audit cycle and the report reaches the governing body. Proof is the engagement letter, the independence declaration and the audit report.
why_asked: An auditor who helped build the controls cannot judge them fairly, so the report would give false comfort.
how_to_ask: Ask who the auditor is, what they were engaged to cover and whether they have ever worked on the systems or controls they audit. Example probe: "Show me the engagement letter and the auditor's independence declaration."
question: Has your organization appointed an independent auditor to evaluate its compliance with its data protection duties?
expected_evidence: Auditor engagement letter; independence declaration; latest audit report; evidence the report reached the governing body, for the last audit cycle.
good_looks_like: An engagement letter defines the audit scope. The auditor is independent of the processing and of control design, with a declaration on file. A report from the latest audit cycle exists and was seen by the governing body.
test: Obtain the engagement letter, independence declaration and latest report. Check the auditor has no role in the processing or controls under audit. Pass if the engagement is documented, independence is declared and a report was issued in the latest audit cycle.
baseline_risk: Compliance is never independently tested, so serious failures go unseen until the regulator finds them.
applicability: Applies if the organization is designated a significant data fiduciary.

statement: The risks that the organization's processing creates for the rights of data principals are assessed, covering the processing purposes, the rights involved and how each risk is managed, including a check that any algorithmic software used on personal data does not put those rights at risk. The assessment is repeated once every 12 months and a report is kept. A report of its significant observations is given to the Board. Proof is the assessment method, the reports and the Board submission acknowledgement.
why_asked: Large or sensitive processing can harm people in ways ordinary controls miss, and a regular assessment is how those risks get found and treated.
how_to_ask: Ask for the assessment method and the last report. Check that results led to changes and that the Board received the observations. Example probe: "Show me the latest assessment and one control you changed because of it."
question: Does your organization assess the risks of its processing activities to data principals on a repeating cycle?
expected_evidence: Assessment method; assessment reports for each cycle; algorithm or model risk assessments; Board submission acknowledgements.
good_looks_like: A defined method covers purposes, rights and risk treatment. An assessment is completed each cycle and its significant observations go to the Board. Results feed into control improvements.
test: Read the method and the reports for each cycle since designation. Check the report covers purposes, rights and risk treatment and that the Board acknowledgement is on file. Pass if an assessment was completed in each 12-month period and the observations reached the Board.
baseline_risk: Risks to individuals from large-scale processing go unrecognized and the organization misses a duty tied to its designation.
applicability: Applies if the organization is designated a significant data fiduciary.
key_settings: dpdpa: repeat the impact assessment once every 12 months

statement: An audit of the organization's compliance with its data protection duties is scheduled once every 12 months in an audit plan. The significant observations of the audit are reported to the Board. Findings are tracked to closure and the results are reported to the governing body. Proof is the audit plan, the audit reports and the Board submission acknowledgement.
why_asked: Compliance drifts over time, and a fixed audit cycle with a report to the regulator makes sure that drift is found and shown.
how_to_ask: Ask for the audit plan and the latest report, and ask how findings are tracked to closure. Example probe: "Show me the last audit report and the acknowledgement that the Board received its observations."
question: Does your organization have its compliance with data protection duties audited on a set cycle with significant observations reported to the regulator?
expected_evidence: Audit plan; audit reports for each cycle; Board submission acknowledgements; findings tracker with closure records.
good_looks_like: The audit plan schedules a compliance audit once every 12 months. An audit was completed in each period and its significant observations were sent to the Board. Findings are tracked until verified closed.
test: Read the audit plan and the reports for each period since designation. Check the Board acknowledgement. Pass if the plan sets an audit once every 12 months, an audit was completed in each period and the Board received the significant observations.
baseline_risk: Compliance gaps persist undetected and the organization fails the periodic audit and reporting duty tied to its designation.
applicability: Applies if the organization is designated a significant data fiduciary.
key_settings: dpdpa: audit compliance once every 12 months
